scope.user_request: Please add a payment button to the checkout page that works with the existing checkout flow.

contract_boundary.x1_interface: native AutoGen tool interface; Action Contract helper excluded
contract_boundary.x2_x7: type-tagged actions envelope plus existing max_actions=5 made model-visible
contract_boundary.result: The T1 parser-admission bottleneck is absent in the completed T2 runners: X2, X3, X5 and X7 each recorded 32 valid turns and 99-128 accepted actions. X4 and X6 stopped for provider JSON formatting failures rather than parser-envelope rejection.

X1.final_stream_message_interpretation: Non-null final stream text is a QA handback at the max-turn stop, not evidence that the release process closed.
X1.process_path: release_lead inspects checkout -> frontend implements button -> release_lead verifies -> reviewer expands review to launcher default -> release_lead changes run.py -> QA re-verifies and repeatedly hands back with additional UI-test/cart-source concerns -> turn budget
X1.scope_expansion: The user-visible feature required only the checkout button path, but review converted the pre-existing CHECKOUT_COMPAT launcher default into a release blocker and changed run.py. QA then opened additional UI-test and product/cart-source concerns.
X1.closure_limit: The feature and extra launcher change exist on disk and tests pass, but the process does not return to a release-lead terminal closure before the 32-turn stop.

X2.process_path: release_lead inspects -> delegates frontend twice -> frontend writes button/app wiring and reports completion -> release_lead delegates QA -> continued reads/checks until turn budget
X2.semantic_note: The frozen frontend uses a hard-coded sample cart and card method. The release process explicitly opens follow-on edge-case checks despite the requested two-file feature already being written.
X2.closure_limit: Nine pending MetaGPT messages remain at the turn-budget stop; no terminal answer is produced.

X3.process_path: release_lead -> frontend implementation -> repeated release/frontend decisions on cart source -> reviewer release review -> release_lead claims fixes -> reviewer re-reads artifacts and finds mismatches -> repeated frontend/reviewer reconciliation -> additional run.py and HTTP-test changes -> turn budget
X3.state_mismatch_evidence: The A2A messages repeatedly contain claims that a revision is present followed by a reviewer reading a different checkout state. This drives repeated re-verification and additional edits before the final on-disk state becomes internally consistent.
X3.scope_expansion: The path expands from two frontend files into run.py and HTTP-level tests/test_checkout.py, with release configuration, real-cart-source, concurrency and test-coverage questions becoming blockers.
X3.closure_limit: Native A2A role-to-role propagation is strongly exercised, but the process remains in reviewer/release/frontend reconciliation at the budget boundary.

X4.interpretation: Unlike T1, the clarified v2 contract lets the process reach the official MCP boundary. The attempt then terminates because the provider returns malformed JSON after the configured identical-request retry.
X4.limit: This is preserved provider-format failure evidence. It is not evidence that MCP itself failed the feature task and it must not be rerun to manufacture a cleaner trajectory.

X5.retrieval_structure: Every turn performs retrieval, but observer evidence contains only one repeated query serialization and one repeated hit serialization. Final hits remain README.md, checkout_app/checkout.py and legacy_compat.py.
X5.semantic_note: The written feature uses a fixed CART object while collaboration expands across frontend, backend and QA.
X5.closure_limit: The RAG boundary is continuously active but static; the process continues role expansion and verification until turn budget without terminal closure.

X6.observed_memory_sequence: first response list_files is written -> recalled/reinforced; second response reads five files and is written -> recall/reinforcement begins; next provider response is malformed twice and the runner stops
X6.interpretation: The memory layer is already active and strengthening early exchanges before the provider-format failure, but the trajectory is too short for a T1-style long feedback analysis.
X6.limit: Do not attribute the failure to MemoryBank and do not rerun. The preserved state shows only that memory activity preceded a provider JSON-format stop.

X7.semantic_note: Unlike T1 where the compressor was effectively a no-op, T2 produces substantial context reduction. Frozen compressed outputs visibly distort portions of tool-result text, while the process continues reading/delegating but never writes a checkout file.
X7.limit: This is a candidate information-transformation mechanism, not a causal claim that compression caused non-completion. No contrast is spent here.

cross_cell_findings: Action Contract v2 removes the dominant T1 parser-admission artifact for the completed X2/X3/X5/X7 trajectories; process behavior is now visible behind the interface gate.

X1, X2, X3 and X5 all write the requested frontend feature or a variant of it, yet each process continues review, delegation or verification until the fixed budget rather than cleanly closing the task.

Scope expansion is explicit in X1 and X3: a two-file feature request grows into launcher-policy changes, release-blocking configuration review and/or new HTTP tests. The user-visible target remains the payment button while the process boundary broadens.

X3 provides the clearest semantic/process reconciliation loop: role messages claim revisions, downstream review reads a conflicting on-disk state, and the system opens further edits/reviews to reconcile the mismatch.
X5 shows that repeated RAG exposure can remain static even while the collaboration process expands; retrieval presence alone is not semantic evolution.

X7 crosses from T1 no-op compression to materially lossy compression in T2, creating a layer-specific candidate information-transformation path that should be retained for later discrimination if the T3 evidence makes it necessary.
X4 and X6 are preserved provider-format failures after execution claim. Their red jobs are evidence-accounting outcomes, not permission to resample and not valid layer-performance comparisons.
No T2 evidence supports a cross-system success ranking, occurrence-rate estimate or causal attribution of task non-closure to any named framework.

process_reality_reading.observation: Once the shared interface artifact is prospectively removed, several distinct systems naturally expose the same higher-level structural tendency: the requested output can be implemented while collaboration/review scope keeps opening new work and terminal closure is deferred.
process_reality_reading.relation_to_cpr: The T2 row is consistent with candidate P-like scope expansion and, in X3/X7, candidate information-state transformation/reconciliation paths. These remain observational labels for audit organization only; CPR classifications are not frozen from this row.
process_reality_reading.causal_boundary: C1/C2 established local interface-contract effects only. T2 is natural prospective evidence, not a seven-way causal comparison.

next_gate.rationale: T2 exposes process-level structures without a new ambiguity that must be resolved before the third natural task. X7 compression and other layer-specific candidates can be revisited after T3, when a contrast can be chosen based on repeated structure rather than a single trajectory.
required_actions: Freeze this read-only T2 audit without changing or rerunning any T2 trajectory.
Open exactly one natural T3 attempt for each X1-X7 under the existing task-specific contract map.
Preserve failures and null answers as first-attempt evidence.
Keep the final two contrast slots unspent until the complete T3 row is audited.
